name: Nimbus Security ShockRing NR-1 'Kiss'
description:
A self-defense ring containing a miniaturized capacitor and twin needle electrodes concealed beneath a decorative bezel. When the wearer rotates the bezel 90 degrees with their opposite hand, the electrodes extend 3mm from the ring's surface, and a slap or grab delivers a 40,000-volt discharge directly into the attacker's skin. The discharge is sufficient to cause involuntary release of a grip, a sharp pain response, and a brief moment of muscle spasm — enough to break free from a grab and create space.

Nimbus Security designed the NR-1 specifically for scenarios where the victim has already been grabbed — a wrist seized, an arm held, a shoulder gripped. In these situations, the ring's electrodes are already in contact with the attacker, and activation is immediate. The ring is available in sizes 5 through 13 and in three metals: surgical steel (Φ95), titanium (Φ140), and a gold-plated variant (Φ260) that is functionally identical but aesthetically premium.

The NR-1 holds eight discharges per charge and recharges via a magnetic contact cradle included with purchase. Its limitation is power — at 40,000 volts with extremely low amperage, it causes pain and surprise but does not incapacitate. Nimbus is explicit in their marketing that the NR-1 buys you one second, and what you do with that second determines the outcome.
specifications: voltage: 40,000V amperage: 2.1 milliamps electrode extension: 3mm from bezel surface discharges per charge: 8 charging: magnetic contact cradle weight: 18 g (steel), 14 g (titanium) sizes: 5-13 cost: Φ95 (steel), Φ140 (titanium), Φ260 (gold-plated) activation: 90-degree bezel rotation
tactical_use: Pre-arm by rotating the bezel before entering high-risk areas. When grabbed, press the ring firmly against the attacker's skin — the palm, inner wrist, or any exposed area. The discharge causes involuntary grip release in most individuals. Immediately pull free and create distance. The NR-1 is a one-second tool — it does not incapacitate, it interrupts. Have a follow-up plan: run, deploy a secondary deterrent, or reach a secure location.
cultural_context: The NR-1 has become particularly popular among women and smaller individuals who are disproportionately targeted for grab-and-hold assaults. Nimbus's marketing features real testimonials from people who credit the ring with helping them escape dangerous situations, and the product has developed a word-of-mouth reputation that outpaces its advertising budget. The gold-plated variant has become a popular gift in Tier 3-4 communities — a 'stay safe' present that doubles as real jewelry.
story_hooks: A modified NR-1 with a data-siphon payload has been found — instead of just shocking the attacker, it injects a micro-charge that reads biometric data from skin contact, harvesting identity information during the defensive discharge.

Nimbus Security's founder was attacked despite wearing an NR-1 and is now funding development of a significantly more powerful successor — the question is whether the new device crosses the line from defense to weapon.

physical_description.visual_profile: A refined, minimalist ring with a slightly raised decorative bezel at the crown. From the front, it appears to be elegant jewelry — understated and professional. The bezel is the only visual indicator of its function: a small rotatable collar that hints at mechanical purpose without screaming 'weapon.' It sits comfortably on the finger, designed to pass as everyday wear.
physical_description.dimensions: Ring diameter: 18-22mm (varies by size 5-13). Bezel height above band: 4mm. Band width: 3.5mm. Electrode extension when activated: 3mm beyond bezel surface.
physical_description.weight_description: Barely noticeable on the hand — the titanium variant (14g) feels almost weightless, while the surgical steel (18g) has a substantial but not burdensome presence. The weight distribution is perfectly balanced across the band, preventing any rotation or drift during wear.
physical_description.primary_material: Surgical steel or titanium band with integrated micro-capacitor housing beneath the surface. Bezel constructed from the same primary material. Internal electrode assembly is surgical-grade stainless with ceramic insulators.
physical_description.finish: Polished surgical steel with a mirror-bright finish; brushed titanium with a matte gunmetal appearance; gold-plated variant with a warm 18k finish. All variants feature a subtle satin finish on the band that resists fingerprints. The bezel rotates with precision, showing minimal play.
physical_description.color_scheme: Steel: silver with subtle gray undertones. Titanium: gunmetal gray with faint iridescent highlights. Gold: warm champagne with platinum accent lines. All variants feature a thin dark line around the bezel rotation point where the mechanical gap sits.
physical_description.grip_texture: The band surface is smooth polished metal — cool to the touch and slightly tacky against bare skin due to micro-texturing. The bezel has precise knurling (fine crosshatch pattern) on its edge to allow secure rotation with the opposite hand's thumb or fingernail.
distinctive_features: Rotatable bezel with mechanical detent — clicks 90 degrees into 'armed' position with tactile feedback
Hairline gap visible around bezel rotation point when rotated — shows mechanical sophistication
Tiny laser-etched charge indicator dots on the inner band (8 dots, one for each discharge) — visible when removed
Minimal branding: 'NIMBUS' engraved in microscopic text on the interior band, nearly invisible without magnification
Electrodes completely concealed beneath bezel when disarmed — no visible openings or seams
Slight luminescence from bezel face in low light — hint of embedded circuitry beneath polished surface
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Nimbus Security logo (stylized cloud symbol Φ) laser-marked on the interior band at the 6 o'clock position. Model designation 'NR-1' appears beside it. On gold-plated variants, hallmark stamps for authenticity appear near the maker's mark.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine when new and well-maintained by its wearer — daily wear shows no degradation. Polished surfaces may show micro-scratches and fingerprints from frequent bezel rotation during pre-arming. Used units may show slight darkening on the electrode contact points from residue, but this is invisible unless the ring is removed and closely inspected.
